behaviour_reference.quote: It also organizes things by turning off or hiding those parts you don't need to see right at the moment; selecting things you need to use all at once, and "locking" layers you don't wish to change with a certain operation.
behaviour_reference.decision: Hide = not visible and not pickable; lock = visible for inspection but protected from change. Both are per layer and take effect at once.

implemented_api_before_this_task: session/layers.rs: set_layer_property(Visible/Locked) and toggle_layer_group; the document already exposed display_attributes with visible/selectable/editable
ui/layers.rs: the lock icon (white/grey) and the visibility slash already reflected the flags
core layers.rs: the Assign arm protected the TARGET layer through editable_layer
gap_found_by_this_task: Moving an object OFF a locked layer was allowed: the target lock was checked, the source lock was not, so a lock only guarded half of the operation (fixture T1, RED 1 passed / 2 failed). Fixed in the controller before any action is planned: a source whose entity or owning layer is locked is refused with Permission("object is on a locked layer"), so the edit costs no transaction.

Pinned, unchanged because they already held: hiding a layer flips display_attributes.visible/selectable and the scene entry at once, a hidden layer offers nothing to select_layer, showing it restores both, and locking keeps the objects visible while making them non-editable.
reuse_decision: ADAPT the 'repaint only what depends on it' habit of gui.rs; ADD the source-side lock rule.
